Definition: adverb from a derivative of G4932; concisely (briefly):--a few words.
BiblicalUsage: Tertullus says, Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious to you, I pray you that you would hear us of your clemency a few words. A few words is all he asks, and the brevity is the courtesy: a short plea before a governor who has no time to waste.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that a few words spoken plainly are worth more than a long speech, and I hold that brevity before authority is a form of respect.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
